class.name: GameplayAbility
class.brief_description: Resource describing an activatable ability and its tag gating.
class.description: Identified by its ability name and optionally bound to an input action. Activation is gated by tags: required tags must be present on the owner, blocked tags must be absent, and owned tags are granted for as long as the ability runs. Extend in GDScript and override [code]_on_give_ability[/code], [code]_can_activate_ability[/code], [code]_activate_ability[/code], [code]_end_ability[/code] and the input hooks. These are virtual methods to override, not signals to connect to.

method.name: _activate_ability
method.description: Override with what the ability actually does. [b]Call [method end_ability] when it is finished[/b] - nothing ends it for you.

method.name: _can_activate_ability
method.description: Override to add your own condition on top of the tag gates: enough stamina, a target in range, off cooldown. Return [code]false[/code] to refuse.

method.name: _end_ability
method.description: Override to clean up. [param was_canceled] is true when something interrupted the ability rather than it running to completion.

method.name: _input_pressed
method.description: Override to react to the driving input going down while the ability is active - a charge starting, a held beam.

method.name: _input_released
method.description: Override to react to the driving input coming up - releasing a charged shot, or ending a held ability.

method.name: _on_give_ability
method.description: Override to set the ability up when it is granted - before it ever activates. Runs once per granted instance.

method.name: _on_remove_ability
method.description: Called when the ability is removed from its component.

method.name: _should_respond_to_event
method.description: Asked before an event in [member trigger_event_tags] activates the ability; return false to ignore this one - a hit for no damage, say. Not asked on the server for a predicted activation the client already started.

method.name: activate_ability
method.description: Starts the ability: grants [member activation_owned_tags], cancels what [member cancel_abilities_with_tag] names, and calls [method _activate_ability]. It does [b]not[/b] re-check [method can_activate_ability], so call that first unless you mean to force it.

method.name: add_gameplay_cue
method.description: Starts a lasting cue from this ability; it is removed when the ability ends (Unreal's default too). See [method execute_gameplay_cue] for why this and not the component's.

method.name: apply_effect_spec_to_owner
method.description: Applies a spec to the owning component.

method.name: apply_effect_to_owner
method.description: Applies [param effect] to the component that owns this ability, returning the same handle as [method AbilitySystemComponent.apply_gameplay_effect_to_self]. This is how an ability spends a cost or applies its own buff.

method.name: apply_effect_to_target
method.description: Applies an effect at this ability's level, with the owner as source, to another component - what an ability that hits something calls.

method.name: can_activate_ability
method.description: Checks the tag gates - [member activation_required_tags], [member activation_blocked_tags], and whether another ability is blocking this one - and then [method _can_activate_ability]. Both have to pass.

method.name: check_cooldown
method.description: Whether none of the cooldown effect's granted tags are owned.

method.name: check_cost
method.description: Whether the cost could be paid: applying the cost effect would leave no attribute below zero. Unreal's CanApplyAttributeModifiers. On a client, it is checked against the values the server last sent.

method.name: commit_ability
method.description: Checks cost and cooldown again and, where effects may be applied, applies both. Returns false - and applies nothing - if either fails. Call it from [method _activate_ability] at the point the ability has really happened, and end the ability if it returns false. On a predicting client it only checks: the cost and the cooldown are applied by the server, and arrive a round trip later.

method.name: commit_ability_cooldown
method.description: Applies only the cooldown.

method.name: commit_ability_cost
method.description: Applies only the cost.

method.name: end_ability
method.description: Ends the ability, releasing its owned tags and calling [method _end_ability]. Pass [code]true[/code] for [param was_canceled] when something interrupted it rather than it finishing. [b]An ability that never calls this stays active and keeps blocking.[/b]

method.name: execute_gameplay_cue
method.description: Fires a one-off cue from this ability. Use this rather than the component's methods inside an ability: on the server's copy of a predicted activation it leaves the owning client out of what is sent - that client already played the cue when it predicted, and through the component directly it would hear it twice. It also adds the avatar as [code]source_path[/code].

method.name: get_ability_id
method.description: This instance's id, unique across every ability granted this run. Granting the same template twice yields two instances with different ids.

method.name: get_ability_level
method.description: The level the ability was granted at; its specs carry it, so level-curve modifiers scale with it.

method.name: get_ability_system_component
method.description: The component this ability was granted to.

method.name: get_active_tasks
method.description: The tasks this activation is running.

method.name: get_avatar
method.description: The node the ability system component hangs off - the pawn root, placed the usual way.

method.name: get_cooldown_tags
method.description: The cooldown effect's granted tags.

method.name: get_cooldown_time_remaining
method.description: Seconds left on this ability's cooldown; 0 when it is ready.

method.name: get_handle
method.description: The id the server gave this ability when it was granted - the same on the server and the owning client, unlike [method get_ability_id].

method.name: get_id_counter
method.description: The counter ids are drawn from. Exposed for tooling; a project has no reason to read it.

method.name: get_is_active
method.description: Whether the ability is running - between [method activate_ability] and [method end_ability].

method.name: get_is_input_pressed
method.description: Whether the input driving this ability is currently held. Maintained by [method input_pressed] and [method input_released].

method.name: get_last_failure_reason
method.description: Why the last activation was refused: [code]&"active"[/code], [code]&"no_owner"[/code], [code]&"blocked"[/code], [code]&"tags"[/code], [code]&"cooldown"[/code], [code]&"cost"[/code], [code]&"script"[/code], or [code]&"rejected"[/code] when the server refused a predicted activation. Empty after a success.

method.name: get_source_object
method.description: Whatever was passed to [method AbilitySystemComponent.give_ability] as the source - the weapon, item or actor that granted the ability. Null when nothing was given.

method.name: get_time_active
method.description: Seconds since the ability was activated; 0 when it is not active.

method.name: get_trigger_event_data
method.description: The payload of the event that started the current activation, or an empty [Dictionary]. On the server's copy of a predicted activation it is what the client sent - check it before trusting it.

method.name: get_trigger_event_tag
method.description: The tag of the event that started the current activation, or empty.

method.name: increment_id_counter
method.description: Advances the id counter. Exposed for tooling; a project has no reason to call it.

method.name: input_pressed
method.description: Tells the ability its input went down; calls [method _input_pressed].

method.name: input_released
method.description: Tells the ability its input came up; calls [method _input_released].

method.name: is_predicting
method.description: True on a client between starting a [constant LOCAL_PREDICTED] activation and the server's answer.

method.name: is_triggered_by
method.description: Whether an event with this tag activates the ability: the tag, or a child of it, is in [member trigger_event_tags].

method.name: make_outgoing_spec
method.description: A spec for [param effect] at this ability's level, with the owner as its source.

method.name: on_give_ability
method.description: Runs the grant-time hook. Called by [method AbilitySystemComponent.give_ability]; override [method _on_give_ability] instead of calling this.

method.name: remove_gameplay_cue
method.description: Removes a cue this ability added before it ends.

method.name: run_task
method.description: Starts a task of your own - an [AbilityTask] subclass - for this activation, and returns it to await. A task started while the ability is not active comes back cancelled, since nothing would ever end it.

method.name: set_ability_level
method.description: Sets the level. Not replicated after the grant.

method.name: set_is_input_pressed
method.description: Sets the held flag by hand. Normally [method input_pressed] and [method input_released] do this.

method.name: setup_ability
method.description: Binds a freshly granted instance to its component and source. [method AbilitySystemComponent.give_ability] calls this; a project does not.

method.name: sync_target_data
method.description: Carries a value from the predicting client to the server's copy of the same activation - an aim, a chosen target. On the predicting client: sends [param data] and completes with it at once. On the server's copy of an activation that client asked for: completes with what the client sent, and [param data] is ignored. Anywhere else (offline, the host's own pawn, an activation the server started): completes with [param data]. The server's result came from a client: check it before trusting it. Calls are matched in order within an activation, so call it the same number of times on both sides.

method.name: wait_all
method.description: Completes when every task in [param tasks] has, with an [Array] of their results in order.

method.name: wait_any
method.description: Completes when the first task in [param tasks] does, with its index; the others are cancelled. Its result is on the task itself.

method.name: wait_attribute_change
method.description: Completes the next time the attribute changes, with a [Dictionary] holding [code]old_value[/code] and [code]new_value[/code].

method.name: wait_delay
method.description: Completes after [param seconds] of physics ticks - the simulation clock, which pauses with the game.

method.name: wait_gameplay_event
method.description: Completes on the next [method AbilitySystemComponent.send_gameplay_event] with this tag, with its payload.

method.name: wait_gameplay_tag_added
method.description: Completes when the owner has the tag (or a child of it) - on the next frame if it already has.

method.name: wait_gameplay_tag_removed
method.description: Completes when the owner no longer has the tag - on the next frame if it already does not.

method.name: wait_input_press
method.description: Completes when the ability's input is pressed, with the seconds waited. On the server's copy of a remote player's ability, presses arrive through the component's own request.

method.name: wait_input_release
method.description: Completes when the ability's input is released, with how long it was held - what a charge attack wants.

members.member: The name [method AbilitySystemComponent.try_activate_ability] looks this ability up by. It has to be unique within one component.
What this ability [i]is[/i]. Other abilities and effects match against these - notably [member cancel_abilities_with_tag] and [member block_abilities_with_tag].
The owner must hold none of these for the ability to activate.
Tags the owner holds for as long as this ability is active. Reference counted, so another source granting the same tag keeps it alive after this ability ends.
The owner must hold every one of these for the ability to activate.
While this ability is active, abilities whose [member ability_tags] match cannot start.
Activating this ability cancels every active ability whose [member ability_tags] match.
A duration effect whose [member GameplayEffect.granted_tags] are the cooldown. The ability cannot activate while its owner has any of them; [method commit_ability] applies it.
An instant effect, normally a negative ADD on a resource attribute. [method can_activate_ability] refuses when it cannot be paid; [method commit_ability] pays it.
The input action [method AbilitySystemComponent.ability_local_input_pressed] routes to this ability. Bind the action on the [Pawn] and forward it; the ability never reads input itself.
Where the ability runs when a networked game activates it. Only matters on a replicated [AbilitySystemComponent]; offline every ability runs where it is activated.

Gameplay events that activate this ability by themselves - Unreal's AbilityTriggers with a GameplayEvent source. [method AbilitySystemComponent.send_gameplay_event] with a matching tag (or a child of one: [code]Event.Hit[/code] is triggered by [code]Event.Hit.Head[/code]) activates the ability with the event's payload, readable through [method get_trigger_event_data]. Events are local to a machine, so where a trigger fires follows Unreal's rule: a [constant LOCAL_PREDICTED] or [constant LOCAL_ONLY] ability is triggered on the machine that controls its owner, a [constant SERVER_ONLY] one on the server. A predicted activation carries the payload to the server with its request, so the server's copy runs with the same data though it never saw the event; an activation claiming an event the ability is not triggered by is refused there.

signal.name: ability_ended
signal.description: Emitted when the ability ends, however it ended.

constants.constant: Runs only on the machine that activated it; the server never hears of it. For purely cosmetic abilities.

The default. The owning client runs it at once and asks the server, which runs it too and confirms - or refuses, and the client's copy is cancelled with [code]&"rejected"[/code]. Its tags are owned on the client at once; its cost and cooldown arrive from the server. When either side ends it, the other side's copy ends too.
The owning client only asks; the server runs it, and the client learns that it is active - its script does not run there. For anything a client must not be trusted to start by itself.
